title: Rebasing addresses
description:
Apply base relocations when a DLL cannot load at its preferred address.

```
preferred base 0x180000000, loaded at 0x7FF900000000
3 pointers fixed:
  0x180003000 -> 0x7FF900003000
  0x180003010 -> 0x7FF900003010
  0x180002F00 -> 0x7FF900002F00
delta = 0x7FF780000000
```
hints: The delta can be thought of as negative when the DLL moves down; unsigned arithmetic wraps and still gives the right answer (lesson 1.02).
Check `offset + 8 <= image.size()` before touching the bytes.

`std::memcpy(destination, source, byteCount)` (from `<cstring>`) copies raw bytes, so it can read an 8-byte pointer out of the byte vector and write it back without worrying about alignment:

```cpp
std::uint64_t value{};
std::memcpy(&value, image.data() + offset, sizeof value);   // read the 8 bytes at offset
value += actual - preferred;
std::memcpy(image.data() + offset, &value, sizeof value);   // write them back
```
requirements: The image is a `std::vector<std::uint8_t>`; the relocation list holds offsets of 8-byte pointers inside it.
Add `actualBase - preferredBase` to each pointer, reading and writing with `std::memcpy`.
Refuse a relocation that would run past the end of the image.
stretch: Parse real relocation blocks: a page RVA, a block size, then 16-bit entries with a type in the top 4 bits.
